entities.summary: Robert d'Ufford, 1st Earl of Suffolk, KG was a powerful English nobleman who played a significant role in the governance of Suffolk during the late 14th century. Born around 1300, d'Ufford was created Earl of Suffolk in 1337 by King Edward III, a position he held until his death in 1369. He was a key figure in the royal administration of the kingdom and was known for his military prowess, particularly during the Hundred Years' War. d'Ufford's legacy extends to the modern era, where he is remembered as a prominent figure in the history of the Earldom of Suffolk. His descendants continued to hold the title until the 19th century, leaving a lasting impact on the region's politics and society. The d'Ufford family's connection to the royal court and their military service during the Hundred Years' War has made them one of the most notable families in Suffolk's history.
